title: The Counter That Counted Nothing
desc: A program that sums numbers with goroutines. The total prints before anyone finishes — if it prints at all.
bugName: Data race on total (plus no WaitGroup)
explain: A triple homicide: concurrent writes with no mutex, one loop variable shared by every goroutine, and zero waiting — main prints before anyone runs. Mutex the shared state, capture the variable, WaitGroup the ending.

title: The Map That Never Was
desc: A word counter. It dies on the very first word.
explain: counts was declared, admired, and never initialized. Reads from a nil map return zero values with a straight face; writes panic on the spot. One word changes everything: make.

title: The Fencepost Felony
desc: Grab the last element of a slice. What could go wrong?
bugName: Index len(s) is out of range
explain: Valid indexes run 0 to len-1, so s[len(s)] panics with total confidence, every single time. The last element lives at s[len(s)-1]. Off-by-one: the oldest bug, still collecting victims.

title: The Connection Vampire
desc: Fetch a URL and print the body. Works fine — until the server stops answering your calls.
explain: Every skipped Close() leaves a connection wandering the dark forever until the transport starves. defer resp.Body.Close() right after the error check — and quit ignoring that error while you are at it.

title: The Append Into the Void
desc: Grow a slice by one. The slice respectfully declines.
explain: append() returned a beautiful longer slice and the code looked away. nums never grew, len never moved, and somewhere a garbage collector is raising the orphan. Catch what append throws: nums = append(nums, 3).

title: The Error That Got Away
desc: Read a file, fall back if it fails. The fallback works. The caller never knows.
explain: := inside the braces minted fresh data AND err, so the outer err kept its original failure and marched out the door with it — while the successful fallback went in the bin. Declare once, assign with =.

title: The Photocopy Romance
desc: Activate every user in the list. Nobody wakes up.
bugName: Mutating the range copy, not the element
explain: range hands you a photocopy of each user and you lovingly activated the photocopy. The real users remain dormant. Hug the original: users[i].Active = true.

title: The Handshake That Never Happens
desc: Send 42 down a channel, then print what comes out. Nothing comes out. Ever.
bugName: Send blocks with no receiver ready
explain: An unbuffered send IS a handshake: it waits for the other hand. The receiver lives on the next line, which cannot run until the handshake finishes. Eternal standoff. Buffer it or receive in a goroutine.

title: The Lock That Locks Nothing
desc: A counter with a mutex. The numbers still come out wrong under load.
explain: The value receiver photocopied the whole struct — padlock included — so every call solemnly locks its own private padlock while the real counter parties on. vet screams copylocks at this. Pointer receiver.

title: The Rescue That Arrived Early
desc: Catch a panic and print saved. The program crashes anyway.
explain: recover only works while a deferred function is running. Here it executed BEFORE the panic, found nothing to rescue, returned nil, and the panic crashed right through it. Wrap it: defer func() { … }().

title: The Field That Does Not Exist
desc: Decode JSON into a struct. One field stays empty no matter what the server sends.
explain: Lowercase fields are invisible to encoding/json no matter how nicely you tag them — name decodes to eternal emptiness. Capitalize it: Name string. The tag cannot save what the compiler cannot see.

title: The Timeout Nobody Set
desc: Give a slow query one second. It takes as long as it wants.
code:
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, time.Second)
defer cancel()
slowQuery()
bugName: ctx never passed to the slow call
explain: A timeout context the work never receives is a fire alarm with no batteries. slowQuery must take ctx and listen for Done(), or the one-second deadline is pure decoration.

title: The Defer Avalanche
desc: Open a thousand files, process each, move on. The OS starts sweating around file 900.
bugName: defers run at function end, not iteration end
explain: defer fires at FUNCTION return, not loop iteration, so every lap stacks another open file onto the pile. A thousand files, a thousand handles, one exhausted OS. Close inline each round.

title: The Case of the Missing .5
desc: Average 7 over 2. Expect 3.5.
explain: int divided by int is int — the .5 was never born. Convert first: float64(total) / float64(n). The compiler watched it happen and said nothing.

title: The Timer Bonfire
desc: Tick once a second while work arrives. The longer it runs, the hotter the garbage collector gets.
explain: Every lap mints a brand-new one-second timer. Spin fast and you are running a timer factory that manufactures garbage. Hoist NewTicker outside, Stop it when done.

title: The Copy Machine From Hell
desc: Build a sentence word by word. Fine for ten words, a tragedy for ten million.
explain: Strings are immutable, so each += retypes the entire manuscript from scratch — O(n squared) suffering on long inputs. strings.Builder does it in one pass and judges you silently.

title: The Error You Chose Not to See
desc: Open a file, read 100 bytes. The file does not exist. Neither, technically, does the program anymore.
bugName: Blanked error, nil file used anyway
explain: That underscore buried file-not-found alive. f is nil, f.Read is a panic in a trenchcoat, and the crime scene points at line 3 instead of line 1. Never blank an error you are about to lean on.

title: The Counter Stuck at Zero
desc: Run three workers, wait for all of them. Main exits before they start.
bugName: Add races with Wait from inside
explain: Add must happen-before Wait, but this Add commutes in from inside the goroutine — Wait can stroll through a zero counter before it arrives. Add(1) BEFORE the go statement. Always.

title: The CPU Bonfire
desc: A loop that waits for work but somehow melts a core doing nothing.
explain: default turns select non-blocking: with nothing ready it spins instantly, forever, at full core. Remove it to park and wait, or rest on time.After.

title: The Lock That Travels
desc: A mutex guarded counter shared with a goroutine. The race detector has opinions.
explain: Passing mu by value clones a live lock — two locks, zero protection, and vet copylocks waving red flags. Pass &mu and share one truth.

title: The Rows That All Match
desc: Three rows appended in a loop. All three print the last values.
bugName: Every row aliases one backing array
explain: append reuses the array while capacity allows, so all three rows point at the same memory holding the LAST write. Fresh allocation or full copy per row.

title: The Half Character
desc: Print the second character of hello with flair. Get modern art instead.
explain: s[1] grabs the second BYTE — the middle of a two-byte é. Range over the string or decode runes to walk actual characters.

title: The Concurrent Map Crash
desc: Ten goroutines, one map, zero locks. Ends in tears.
explain: Maps are not thread-safe: concurrent writes crash with a fatal error that recover cannot catch. Mutex it, shard it, or use sync.Map.

title: The Silent Closer
desc: Create a file, defer its close, write away. The path does not exist.
bugName: Blanked error, nil file used anyway
explain: The blanked error hid the missing file, so BOTH the deferred Close and the Read operate on nil. Check err first — defer still runs on early return, that is its whole job.

title: The Edge Thief
desc: A binary search that works everywhere except the last slot. Hunting 38 prints 'Not found' while 38 sits right there at index 6.
bugName: Loop quits before the last check (needs <=)
explain: for low < high stops when the borders meet — but one remaining slot still needs checking. The lone < steals the edge; <= gives it back.

title: Drawers Made of Thin Air
desc: A frequency counter that panics on its very first write. The map looks declared and ready.
explain: var m map[...]... is nil: reading gives zero values all day, but writing needs real drawers. make() it or use a literal first.

title: The Self Match
desc: A one-pass two sum that answers '1 1' — one item marrying itself. The pair it should find is sitting right there.
bugName: Files before asking — item finds itself
explain: Storing v before checking lets 5 find ITSELF whenever the target is double one item. Ask the drawer first, file second.

title: One Slot Too Far
desc: A printer that walks seven slots and falls off the end. Seven prints, then a panic.
explain: Valid slots run 0 to len-1. The <= allows len itself — Go panics instead of handing you the neighbor's memory.
